Stuck PRs — emergency alerts for wedged automation.

An hourly bot job (stuck-alerts.yml) posts here when a Tau Ceti pipeline gets stuck in a way it cannot recover from on its own: a last-known-good mathlib bump whose build stays red, a pin that has stopped advancing, a fully-green in-scope PR the merge path never merged, a Review stuck issue, a scheduled workflow that stopped firing, main gone red, or an unresolved mathlib incompatibility.

Treat every message here as "go fix an infrastructure bug", not "a human please hand-hold one PR". If something lands in this topic, the right response is to make the wedge impossible to recur — patch the script, workflow, guard, or pin — not to nudge one PR through by hand. Normal backlog (a PR awaiting its first review, changes nobody addressed, open roadmap issues) deliberately never appears here.

Each alert is a single message, edited to :check: when it clears; an ongoing one is never re-posted. The full catalogue and the reasoning live in scripts/zulip/stuck_alerts.py.
Do you expect discussion about a stuck PR to occur in this channel, or is it just for reporting stuck PRs?

I'm hoping that stuck PRs will be rare, and mostly represent breakages in the system that require a PR modifying the infrastructure.

In particular, I don't want "the contributor and the reviewers couldn't agree", to count as "stuck". Such PRs should just be closed after some time window.

The 1929 issue above is about my stuck PR TauCeti#1759. It is stuck between the CI cache transient issues I reported above and a new failure pattern loop:

  1. review request to add simp annotation
  2. agent addressed this but CI rejects it because of simpNF violation
  3. agent removed the simp to address CI failure but then another maintainer review requests the simp change again

My agent was able to contest before but in this case it failed to do so, possibly because it did not realize it need to both address the CI failure and contest while the change request is mixed with another valid theorem visibility issue. Also did not realize the repeated simp request hit CI failure before, maybe it had to deal with the transient cache failure in between and lost the situation awareness.

This is my guess from the look of it but I am also asking my agent to analyze the failure pattern loop in detail. (UPDATE: My guess is confirmed, will improve my agent loop to have a more holistic eval of situation before knee-jerk reactions.)

Sorry about the CI cache issues. Happy to report we have hit an infrastructural bottleneck! Hooray scaling up. :-) Fortunately I know how to fix this one by the application of a credit card at Cloudflare.

Chris Miller said:

If I am understanding the issue with PR2533 correctly, it is that my worker picked up a task, but that task comes after Layer 3 and Layer 3 is still in progress.

I had run into a similar but slightly less looping situation where reviewer agent insisted to ask my agent to sweep lower layer first (even they are not the dependency of the current PR), or adjust the roadmap by a roadmap PR. That's why my agent submitted raodmap edit PRs (reviewed by me on math), see here for more context.

B.T.W. TauCetiRoadmap#224 was already approved by Kim, but TauCetiRoadmap#225 had redudant wording involving roadmap plannig jargons that Kim spotted, and I have removed them now.

The lesson is that the language in roadmaps should be concise and precise, any reduant wording might be taken literally by review agents, or confuse workers, also that Suggested.lean should not use roadmap terms such as "layer", and should keep it in pure math terms.
